messages.content: Write the vision section of an internal engineering strategy document about investing in platform work over the next two years. Around 250 words.

output:
## Vision

Two years from now, shipping a new service here should be boring.

Right now it isn't. A team starting something new spends its first three or four weeks on work nobody asked for: wiring up auth, copying a CI config from whichever repo looked healthiest, guessing at how to get metrics into a dashboard, discovering on the day of launch that the deploy path has an undocumented manual step. Every team pays this tax, and every team pays it slightly differently, which is why we now maintain six variations of the same retry logic.

The bet is simple. We put a small number of engineers on the paths everyone walks — build, deploy, observability, data access — and treat those paths as products with users, owners, and a support burden. Not a side project someone picks up between features.

What we want on the other side: a new service in production the same week it's scoped. One deploy pipeline, not a genre of them. An on-call engineer who can find the cause of an incident without knowing which team wrote the code. And enough shared ground that a person moving between teams is useful on day two.

This costs real capacity. Roughly eight engineers, sustained, who would otherwise be building features — and the first year will feel like pure overhead, because it mostly is. We think the trade is right anyway. We are spending more on internal friction today than the platform team would cost, we're just spending it in a form that doesn't appear on any roadmap.

---
